title: Lone Working Safety
blurb: How to work alone safely: tell someone, stay secure, avoid high-risk tasks, and put your safety first.
siteNotes: Who to tell, and how to check in, when opening or closing alone
How help is raised quickly at each site (phone, alarm, nearest colleague)
Which tasks are not to be done alone
legalNotes: Employers must assess risks and put sensible precautions in place, which includes lone working: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, reg. 3. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3242 (HSE guidance says lone working is not banned in general).
No CHECK items. The trainer correctly says lone working is not banned.

cards.title: Lone Working Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- make sure someone knows where you are and when you finish
- keep yourself secure while alone
- put your safety before property

cards.title: Not banned, but it needs thought
cards.body: There will be times you work on your own: opening up early, closing down late, cleaning a quiet area, or being the only one in the office. Lone working is not banned, but if something goes wrong there is no colleague right there to help.

cards.title: Someone must know
cards.body: The most important thing is that someone knows. Make sure another person knows you are on site and roughly when you expect to finish, and agree a way to check in. Keep a phone on you at all times.

cards.title: Keep doors secured, avoid risky jobs
cards.body: Keep external doors secured and do not let unknown callers in. Deliveries and visitors can wait or be verified. Some tasks are much better done when someone else is around.

left.title: Do
items: Verify callers or ask them to wait
Save risky tasks for when others are in

cards.title: Your safety comes first
cards.body: Your personal safety always comes before the premises, the stock or the takings. If you feel unsafe or threatened, remove yourself from the situation and call for help. Do not try to be a hero to protect property.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Someone must know you are on site and when you will finish
- Keep a phone on you at all times
- Keep external doors secured and do not admit unknown callers
- Avoid cellar drops, working at height and large cash handling alone
- Your personal safety comes before property, stock and takings

cards.q: What is the most important thing to arrange before working alone?
options: A full list of the day's expected deliveries and callers
A written plan covering every task for the whole shift
A spare set of keys for the premises and the safe
That someone knows you are on site and when you finish
cards.why: Make sure another person knows you are on site and roughly when you expect to finish, and agree a way to check in.

cards.q: You should keep a phone on you when lone working.
cards.why: It lets you raise the alarm and be contacted.

cards.q: When alone, unknown callers at the door should be…
options: Not admitted, but verified or asked to wait
Given a key to wait inside
Sent round to a side door
Let straight in so they are not left outside
cards.why: Deliveries and visitors can wait or be verified.

cards.q: Higher-risk tasks like cellar drops are best avoided when you are alone.
cards.why: Cellar drops, working at height and handling large amounts of cash are better done when someone else is around.

cards.q: When lone working, external doors should be…
options: Propped open so you can hear callers
Kept secured
Left unlocked for deliveries
Left on the latch for staff arriving
cards.why: Keep external doors secured when you are alone.

cards.q: Your personal safety comes before the premises, stock or takings.
cards.why: This is the golden rule of lone working.

cards.q: If you feel unsafe or threatened while alone, what should you do?
options: Confront them so they back off
Lock yourself in and wait until morning
Stay put and guard the takings
Remove yourself from the situation and call for help
cards.why: Do not try to protect property at your own risk. Remove yourself and call for help.

cards.q: You should try to be a hero and protect property even at risk to yourself.
cards.why: Do not try to be a hero to protect property.

cards.q: Handling large amounts of cash is…
options: Fine as long as you keep your phone on you
Best done alone, so nobody knows
Better done when someone else is around
Fine any time if the doors are locked
cards.why: Large amounts of cash are better handled when someone else is around.

cards.q: Lone working is completely banned at all times.
cards.why: It is not banned, but it needs extra thought because there is no colleague right there to help.
